placements.why: This envelope's content is organized around a deployment pipeline requirement (signed release manifest) that spans environments and is codified as a standing rule, not a single decision. Nothing in the supplied (empty) strata covers infrastructure/process governance, and this is exactly the shape of category the org's strata taxonomy is meant to hold, so it is minted as the top-level home for release-pipeline structural requirements.
placements.title: Release infrastructure gains enforceable structural preconditions
placements.frame: Does this content define a standing structural requirement for how the system is built, verified, or released — rather than a one-off operational decision or event?

placements.title: Deployment safety becomes a structural precondition rather than a discretionary check
placements.frame: Is the signed-manifest gate being treated as a standing precondition the release pipeline itself enforces, and what precedent or scope is invoked to justify or extend its reach?
placements.why: src-1 (Quinton's spoken directive), src-3/src-4/src-5 (the memo's Gate/Scope/Owner fields) all state the same theme in different registers: a signed release manifest is now a mandatory precondition for Meridian deploys, scoped to staging and production, owned by a named role. src-2 is not its own theme — per the narrative grain test it is a one-time incident fact ('two unsigned artifacts reached staging last quarter') that evidences why the gate exists, so it joins this leaf's support as justification rather than minting separately. Together these name a subject future envelopes will keep feeding (gate evolution, scope changes, ownership transfer, incidents that test it), not a single fact.
